Submits one or more named scores for a function run, or for specific steps when step IDs are provided. Scores are recorded as run metadata and aggregated for experiments.

parameters.description: Run ID (ULID) of the function run to score
parameters.name: runId

schema.description: Scores to record for the run. The REST request body is this array. Writes are applied in order and are not atomic; if a later score fails, earlier scores may already be recorded. Score writes are best-effort: run and step targets are not validated before writing, and scores for targets that do not exist may not surface in queries. Maximum 100 scores.

apiHttpBody.description: A message that represents an arbitrary HTTP body.

contentType.description: The HTTP Content-Type header value specifying the content type of the body.

data.description: The HTTP request/response body as raw binary.

extensions.description:
Application specific response metadata. Must be set in the first response
for streaming APIs.

@type.description:
A URL/resource name that uniquely identifies the type of the serialized
protocol buffer message. This string must contain at least
one "/" character. The last segment of the URL's path must represent
the fully qualified name of the type (as in
`path/google.protobuf.Duration`). The name should be in a canonical form
(e.g., leading "." is not accepted).

In practice, teams usually precompile into the binary all types that they
expect it to use in the context of Any. However, for URLs which use the
scheme `http`, `https`, or no scheme, one can optionally set up a type
server that maps type URLs to message definitions as follows:

* If no scheme is provided, `https` is assumed.
* An HTTP GET on the URL must yield a [google.protobuf.Type][]
  value in binary format, or produce an error.
* Applications are allowed to cache lookup results based on the
  URL, or have them precompiled into a binary to avoid any
  lookup. Therefore, binary compatibility needs to be preserved
  on changes to types. (Use versioned type names to manage
  breaking changes.)

Note: this functionality is not currently available in the official
protobuf release, and it is not used for type URLs beginning with
type.googleapis.com. As of May 2023, there are no widely used type server
implementations and no plans to implement one.

Schemes other than `http`, `https` (or the empty scheme) might be
used with implementation specific semantics.

protobufNullValue.description:
`NullValue` is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the
`Value` type union.

The JSON representation for `NullValue` is JSON `null`.

 - NULL_VALUE: Null value.

archivedAt.description: Timestamp when the app was archived (if archived)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the app was first synced

functionCount.description: Number of functions in the app

appVersion.description: App version reported by the latest sync, if set

error.description: Most recent sync or connectivity error for the app, if any

framework.description: Framework used by the app, if reported by the SDK

sdkLanguage.description: Language of the SDK that synced the app

sdkVersion.description: Version of the SDK that synced the app

status.description: Status of the latest sync. `success` and `duplicate` are successful terminal states. `duplicate` means the sync payload matched the previous successful sync, so no function configuration changes were applied. `error` is a failed terminal state, and `pending` means the sync is still in progress.

syncedAt.description: Timestamp for the latest sync, if available

url.description: URL of the Inngest endpoint in the app, if synced via URL

name.description: Score name; must be at most 128 UTF-8 bytes

stepId.description: Optional SDK step ID; attaches the score to a specific step instead of the run. Step targets are recorded best-effort and are not validated before writing.

value.description: Score value; must be a finite number or a boolean

response.description: Optional inline JS function which is called to respond to GET requests
response.example: function respond(body, headers) { return { status: 200, headers: {}, body: JSON.parse(body)?.challenge } };

transform.description: The inline JS transform function for incoming events
transform.example: function transform(evt, headers = {}, queryParams = {}, raw = '') { return { name: 'webhook/request.received', data: evt }; }

events.description: Allow or deny specific events, e.g. 'orders/payment.created', or 'orders/*' for all orders. Only events in this list will be either allowed or denied.

code.description: Machine-readable code representing the type of diagnostic

context.description: Snippet of the query string around the position to provide context for the diagnostic

end.description: Ending character index in the query string where the diagnostic applies

start.description: Starting character index in the query string where the diagnostic applies

schema.description: JSON Schema describing the shape of this event's data, represented as a nested JSON object

name.description: Name of the column in the insights query result

values.description: Values for a single row of the insights query result, where each value corresponds to a column. The value is represented as a JSON object to allow for flexible typing (e.g., string, number, boolean, etc.)

description.description: Human-readable description of the table and its contents

name.description: Name of the table, used when writing queries

description.description: Human-readable description of the column and the data it contains

name.description: Name of the column in the insights table

type.description: Data type of the column (e.g., 'String', 'Int64', 'Array(String)', etc.)

completedAt.description: Timestamp when the function execution completed (if finished)

error.description: Error message if the function execution failed

queuedAt.description: Timestamp when the function execution was enqueued

result.description: JSON string containing the function result (only available for completed synchronous invocations)

runId.description: Unique identifier for this function execution

startedAt.description: Timestamp when the function execution started (if started)

data.description: Paginated list of event type schemas
List of available tables that can be queried via the Insights query endpoint

columns.description: Column metadata for the insights query result

diagnostics.description: Any non-fatal diagnostics related to the insights query execution

rows.description: Rows of the insights query result, where each row contains a list of values corresponding to the columns

sql.example: SELECT function_id, COUNT(*) AS total, countIf(status = 'Failed') AS failures, failures / total AS failure_rate FROM function_runs WHERE started_at >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY GROUP BY function_id ORDER BY failure_rate DESC LIMIT 10

summary.description: A natural language summary of the generated query, useful for explaining the query's intent to agents
summary.example: This query retrieves the top 10 functions with the highest failure rate over the past week, showing the total number of runs, number of failures, and calculated failure rate for each function.

prompt.description: Natural language description of the query to generate
prompt.example: Show me the top 10 functions by failure rate in the last 7 days

query.description: The insights query to execute, written in modified ClickHouse SQL

runId.description: New run ID created by the rerun

input.description: Optional replacement step input as a JSON array

stepId.description: User-defined step name to rerun from

runId.description: Run ID the score was recorded against

stepId.description: Step ID the score was recorded against, if step-scoped

eventId.description: Internal event ID assigned by Inngest

id.description: Optional event ID used for idempotency when scheduling function runs

ts.description: Optional event timestamp as Unix time in milliseconds. Defaults to the current time.

user.description: Deprecated user data. Put user data in the data field instead.

status.description: Status of the sync. `success` and `duplicate` are successful terminal states. `duplicate` means the sync payload matched the previous successful sync, so no function configuration changes were applied. `error` is a failed terminal state, and `pending` means the sync is still in progress.
